video.title: How Shoulder Rotation Syncs Your Contact

classification.reason: The coach analyzes the biomechanics of forehand contact timing across different players and explains how to sync contact with internal shoulder rotation.

problem.title_as_question: How does shoulder rotation synchronize your forehand contact point?
problem.definition: Players struggle with contact timing and burying balls because they try to hit at an arbitrary spatial contact point rather than matching contact to the exact onset of their individual internal shoulder rotation.
problem.target_player: Players struggling with inconsistent contact timing or trying to force an unnatural contact point

symptoms.description: The ball is buried straight into the ground.
Racket face angle turns over excessively and faces downward at contact.
Swing feels jammed, awkward, or painful at contact.

causes.statement: The player hits the ball at a location in space that fails to match the exact transition point where their shoulder rolls forward.
The shoulder has already rolled forward too much prior to contact, altering the racket angle so the ball cannot be hit cleanly.
The player attempts to copy an arbitrary extended forward contact point even though their natural shoulder biomechanics release earlier closer to the body.

angles.summary: Every forehand must be struck right at the start of internal shoulder rotation because rotating forward too early destroys the string angle.
There is no single objective contact point in space; proper contact point is individual and determined by when the shoulder transitions into forward roll.
Swiatek releases early with a bent elbow closer to the body, whereas Federer holds external rotation longer and releases far out in front.
Demonstrating that if an early-releasing player like Kyrgios tried to hit at Federer's contact point, the racket face would shut and drive the ball into the ground.
Shoulder release timing is an intuitive natural feeling of when the shoulder stops stretching and releases forward, rather than a calculated millisecond window.

solutions.summary: Take a comfortable, painless pressing shadow swing to observe and locate the exact spot where your shoulder has just started to turn over.
Use your feet and eyes to actively receive the ball into your identified release spot, then fire and let the shoulder go.
